Cinnamon Atole

Served at: Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation)

Serves 4-6Prep 10 minCook 20-25 min

Cinnamon Atole is a warm, thick, and comforting beverage, often made from masa (corn dough) or masa harina, milk, and spices. It's a staple in Mexican cuisine, especially during colder months and festive occasions. On Candlemas (Día de la Candelaria) on February 2nd, it's traditionally served alongside tamales, marking the end of the Christmas season and the presentation of Jesus at the Temple.

Ingredients

  • 1/2 cup (60 g) masa harina for tortillas
  • 4 cups (960 ml) whole milk, divided
  • 1 cup (240 ml) water
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) piloncillo (Mexican brown sugar cone), chopped, or 1/2 cup (100 g) packed light brown sugar
  • 2 cinnamon sticks (about 3 inches or 7.5 cm each)
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • Optional: 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract

Method

  1. In a medium bowl, whisk together the masa harina with 1 cup (240 ml) of the milk until smooth and no lumps remain. Set aside.
  2. In a large saucepan or pot, combine the remaining 3 cups (720 ml) milk, water, piloncillo (or brown sugar), cinnamon sticks, and salt.
  3. Heat the mixture over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the piloncillo or brown sugar has completely dissolved and the mixture is warm, but not boiling.
  4. Slowly pour the masa harina mixture into the saucepan, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
  5. Continue to cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently with a whisk or wooden spoon, for 15-20 minutes, or until the atole thickens to your desired consistency (it should be like a thin gravy or thick hot chocolate). Be careful not to let it scorch at the bottom.
  6. Remove the cinnamon sticks. If using, stir in the vanilla extract.
  7. Serve hot in mugs.

Tips

  • For a thinner atole, add a little more milk or water until desired consistency is reached.
  • Atole can be made with various flavorings like chocolate (Champurrado), fruit purees, or nuts.
  • Always stir frequently while cooking to prevent lumps and sticking to the bottom of the pot.
